title: Griffin Cloud x Redwood intro & integration discovery
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and Griffin Cloud. Griffin is a regional cloud/GPU provider exploring a go-to-market partnership and potential integration paths (marketplace, dedicated GPU offering, private deployment bundle). Key concerns: integration effort, customer SLAs, KMS support, VPC peering, pricing split, and pilot benchmarks. Agreed next steps: share partner one-pager + security pack, schedule technical deep dive for infra/DevOps, and set up pilot with 2 customers for benchmarking.
topics: Partner GTM options (marketplace vs reseller vs referral)
Technical integration options: API, Dedicated pools, Private deployments (VPC/air-gapped)
Security/compliance: SOC2, SSO, KMS/HSM, audit logs
Commercials: pricing split, reserved capacity, pilot credits
Operational: onboarding flow, billing integration, support & SLAs

transcript:
[00:00] Samir Rao: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Samir from Griffin Cloud here. Quick roll call.
[00:05] Avery Chen: Hi Samir, Avery from Redwood, AE. With me: Maya (SE) and Jordan from partner ops.
[00:12] Maya Patel: Hey all.
[00:18] Elena Varga: Elena, infra. Diego and Priya are here too.
[00:24] Diego Morales: yep, hello.
[00:30] Priya Singh: Priya - security.
[01:02] Avery Chen: Cool, agenda — quick intros, high level partnership goals, technical integration options, security questions, then next steps. Sound good?
[01:10] Samir Rao: Yep. We're exploring partnerships to offer ML inference as a managed option to our enterprise customers. We run multi-tenant Kubernetes clusters and also offer dedicated GPU instances. Main ask: how would Redwood slot into our stack and what's required from Griffin.
[01:40] Maya Patel: high level — Redwood provides hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private deployments (VPC/on-prem). For a partner like Griffin, common options are 1) marketplace listing to resell hosted API, 2) joint dedicated offering where we place dedicated pools on your infra, or 3) private deployment where Redwood control plane is separate and model inference runs in your VPC.
[02:20] Elena Varga: when you say private deployment — do you mean we host the model runtime entirely in our network? Any control plane calls go out? We have strict egress rules.
[02:40] Maya Patel: good question. We support a private control plane option where control signals — deployments, metrics — can be routed through a customer-managed control plane. For air-gapped customers we can bundle an on-prem package. There is some optional telemetry but we can disable egress if needed. We also support KMS integrations so keys never leave customer env.
[03:05] Priya Singh: that's encouraging. We need SOC2 level evidence and details on KMS/HSM and audit logs. Also SSO/SAML for partner admin.
[03:22] Avery Chen: yes, we'll share a security pack. We have SOC2 report and details on SSO, RBAC, and KMS integrations. We can also walk through logging retention and audit trails.
[03:35] Diego Morales: on infra — Griffin provides dedicated GPU instances (A100/V100-equivalent) and we also have a managed Kubernetes offering. For the Dedicated pool model, how much customization is needed?
[03:55] Maya Patel: for dedicated pools we typically stage GPU nodes and a runtime that Redwood deploys. We can work with your ops team to tune kernels/compilers. The usual integration points: node-level drivers, container runtime, and network peering for API traffic. If you want us to manage the runtime, we need admin access to deploy. Alternatively we can provide a self-managed operator.
[04:30] Elena Varga: admin access is tricky for some customers. Self-managed operator is preferable. How mature is that operator?
[04:46] Maya Patel: it's been used in a few private deployments, but we do recommend a short pilot and runbook. We can provide helm charts and an operator image. Some edge cases around kernel/quantization need SE input.
[05:05] Samir Rao: Let's talk GTM — revenue split, marketplace fees — do you have standard partner tiers?
[05:17] Jordan Ruiz: Redwood has a partner program: referral, reseller, and co-sell. For reseller/marketplace deals, we have standard commercial templates but we can negotiate reserved capacity discounts for strategic partners. We typically offer partner credits for pilots.
[05:38] Samir Rao: pilots — we want to run benchmarks on latency and cost against our existing offerings and Lambda Labs-like providers. Any benchmark tooling?
[05:50] Maya Patel: yes, we have benchmark scripts and can run end-to-end throughput/latency tests with KV cache enabled, sequence-length distributions, and batching profiles. We'll want 24-48 hour windows for steady-state.
[06:10] Diego Morales: do you support multi-tenant isolation? We have customers who need strong tenant separation.
[06:20] Maya Patel: Dedicated pools provide isolation; private deployments give you full tenant isolation. Our hosting model is multi-tenant but offers quotas and role-based access.
[06:35] Priya Singh: encryption at rest and in transit — KMS support? HSM?
[06:42] Avery Chen: we integrate with major KMS providers (AWS KMS, Google KMS, Azure Key Vault) and can support customer-managed keys and HSM workflows for private deployments.
[06:56] Elena Varga: networking — for hosted API, customers will need peering or VPN. We prefer VPC peering for lower latency. Does Redwood support cross-account VPC peering?
[07:10] Maya Patel: Yes, we have a VPC peering and private link setup for hosted or dedicated connections. For private deployments, everything is in your VPC so no peering needed.
[07:25] Samir Rao: Any restrictions on model variants or quantization? Some of our customers want to run extremely large LLMs.
[07:35] Maya Patel: runtime supports many open models; for very large models we recommend dedicated pools with GPU types that match memory needs. We also support quantized variants; kernel selection is automatic but we may recommend a specific quantization profile for cost tradeoffs.
[07:58] Diego Morales: latency numbers — can you share ballpark p99 for a 2k token sequence on A100s and on your hosted tier?
[08:12] Maya Patel: ballpark: dedicated tuned A100 pools with optimized kernels — p99 could be ~800-1200ms for 2k tokens depending on batching. Hosted tier varies; with batching/prefix cache you can often get single-client latency ~300-600ms for typical prompts but multi-tenant bursty workloads will be higher. These are rough estimates; we'll run the benchmark.
[08:45] Priya Singh: SLAs — what's typical uptime and latency SLOs for dedicated customers?
[08:53] Avery Chen: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime (99.9%+) and target latency SLOs. For enterprise deals we include on-call support and runbook commitments.
[09:05] Samir Rao: billing integration — some of our customers want to have unified billing through Griffin. Can Redwood do reseller billing where we collect and pay you?
[09:18] Jordan Ruiz: yes, reseller flows are supported. We integrate via invoicing or marketplace billing; we can discuss specifics and sample contract language.
[09:30] Elena Varga: operationally, what is onboarding timeline for a private deployment vs dedicated pool?
[09:40] Maya Patel: private deployment pilot: ~3-6 weeks (operator install, basic validation, pilot run). Dedicated pool onboarding depends on capacity availability and provisioning — often 2-4 weeks if hardware is available. Marketplace listing can be immediate once paperwork is done.
[10:05] Samir Rao: what partner enablement materials do you have? decks, integration docs, runbooks?
[10:12] Avery Chen: we'll share a partner one-pager, integration docs, an operations runbook, and a security pack. Also sample benchmark scripts and a partner playbook.
[10:25] Diego Morales: for the pilot, can we co-run with two of our customers? We want to validate both multi-tenant and dedicated flows.
[10:34] Jordan Ruiz: absolutely. We recommend one customer for hosted/Dedicated proof-of-concept and another for private deployment if possible. We'll provide credits and engineering time for the pilot.
[11:00] [Cross talk / brief overlap] Samir Rao: timeline-wise, if we start the pilot by November, is that realistic?
[11:10] Maya Patel: yes, we can get the pilot plan drafted and a benchmark runbook in the next 10 days.
[11:18] Priya Singh: a few security clarifications: Do you rotate keys automatically? What's retention for logs?
[11:27] Avery Chen: key rotation supported via KMS rotation or manual triggers; logs retention is configurable — default 90 days but extended retention is an add-on. We'll include exact policies in the security pack.
[12:00] Samir Rao: any legal/compliance checklist for marketplace listing?
[12:06] Jordan Ruiz: we have a partner contract template and marketplace terms; legal review usually takes 2-3 weeks depending on counters. We can share templates.
[12:22] Elena Varga: one technical ask — we'd like to see a short demo of the operator and a simple benchmark. Can we schedule a separate SE-led deep dive?
[12:33] Maya Patel: yes, SE deep dive. We'll include operator install steps, sample helm values, and a bench script that tests batching, KV cache, and sequence-length variance.
[12:48] Diego Morales: on the model side — do you manage the model catalog or can we bring custom customer models?
[12:56] Maya Patel: both. Customers can bring their own models; we support onboarding custom model artifacts. For hosted model catalog, Redwood curates open models and maintains performance profiles.
[13:10] Samir Rao: great. Any major blockers you see for go/no-go on a partnership?
[13:18] Avery Chen: none immediate; main dependencies are security review, pilot success, and commercial terms.
[13:25] Priya Singh: we'll need SOC2 and the KMS/HSM diagrams before presenting to our security committee.
[13:32] Avery Chen: will share those.
[13:40] Samir Rao: ok let's recap next steps.
[13:45] Avery Chen: recap: Redwood sends partner one-pager + security docs (Avery). Maya schedules SE deep dive with Elena and Diego. Jordan drafts pilot commercial. Griffin shares network topology and sample customer use cases.
[14:02] Elena Varga: I'll send topology and a contact for each pilot customer.
[14:10] Diego Morales: timeline sounds good.
[14:20] Samir Rao: thanks everyone. We'll reconvene after review.
[14:28] Avery Chen: thanks, speak soon.

Note: transcript is auto-transcribed; occasional mislabels and minor word swaps observed (e.g., 'KV cache' transcribed as 'K V cache' in places). Links shared: partner one-pager (link will be emailed), security pack (SOC2, KMS diagrams), benchmark script (repo link).
